# Fastfile for the Fa app (flutter_app).
#
# TestFlight submit lanes, adapted 1:1 from learn.ai's deploy setup: builds
# happen in the CI workflows (flutter build ipa / flutter build macos), so
# these lanes only upload the produced artifacts with the App Store Connect
# API key from the environment:
#
# The daily's submit_only lanes distribute straight to the EXTERNAL
# TestFlight group (issue #239): the group name and Beta App Review contact
# ride repo variables (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_*,
# BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL). release-appstore.yml drives the manual
# submit_for_review lanes (App Store review submission).
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID / APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID /
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT
#
# Android (#289): the build_only/build_release + upload_only lanes follow
# the same split against Google Play; the service-account JSON rides
# PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON and
# the track rides PLAY_TRACK (internal first, then external beta).
#
# iOS:    IOS_IPA_PATH points at the built .ipa (default: build/ios/*.ipa's
#         conventional location).
# macOS:  MACOS_PKG_PATH points at the signed .pkg (Mac Installer
#         Distribution cert) and MACOS_BUNDLE_ID overrides dev.fa1.app.

require_relative "appstore_preflight"
require_relative "play_listing_sync"
require_relative "play_upload_preflight"
require_relative "store_version_create"
require_relative "version_floor"

def asc_api_key
  app_store_connect_api_key(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key_content: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"],
    is_key_content_base64: false,
    in_house: false
  )
end

# App Store locale map for the store pipeline: fastlane/metadata folder →
# App Store Connect locale. Golden screenshots live one level below under
# the plain language code (test/goldens/store/<en|ru>/<ios|ipad|mac>).
def store_locale_map
  { "en-US" => "en-US", "ru-RU" => "ru" }
end

# Latest "## [version]" section of store_artefacts/metadata/<lang>/changelog.md.
def store_latest_changelog(lang)
  file_path = File.expand_path("../../store_artefacts/metadata/#{lang}/changelog.md", __dir__)
  return "" unless File.exist?(file_path)
  content = File.read(file_path)
  match = content.match(/## \[.*?\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=\n## \[|\z)/m)
  match ? match[1].strip : ""
end

# gh-1522: the version string every store lane reports/verifies. The
# derived BUILD_NAME env (build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml version job,
# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# ── External TestFlight distribution (issue #239) ─────────────────────────
# A missing repo variable is a LOUD named failure at lane start (AC1) —
# never a fastlane stack trace mid-upload. The variables are set once as
# repo variables and passed through by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml.
def require_env!(name, what)
  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

def external_testflight_group!
  require_env!("TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP",
               "external TestFlight distribution needs the group name (create the 'External Beta' group in App Store Connect, then set the TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP repo variable)")
end

# Beta App Review contact (AC2): external distribution only flips green
# unattended when the review info is complete. The app is local-first —
# it boots without any account or key, so no demo account is required.
def beta_app_review_info!
  {
    contact_first_name: ENV.fetch("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_FIRST_NAME", "Uladzimir"),
    contact_last_name: ENV.fetch("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_LAST_NAME", "Klyshevich"),
    contact_email: require_env!("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL", "Beta App Review needs a contact email (set the BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL repo variable)"),
    contact_phone: require_env!("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE", "Beta App Review needs a contact phone (set the BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE repo variable)"),
    demo_account_required: false,
    notes: "Local-first AI agent app. No account, sign-in or API key is required — the app boots fully on-device with local models, so there is nothing to sign into."
  }
end

def beta_app_feedback_email!
  require_env!("BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL", "external TestFlight testing needs a feedback email (set the BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL repo variable)")
end

# distribute_external requires a "What to Test" changelog — pilot raises in
# non-interactive CI without one. Reuse the store release notes.
def testflight_changelog
  notes = store_latest_changelog("en")
  notes.empty? ? "Bug fixes and improvements." : notes
end

# Bounded wait for ASC processing (E1): external distribution needs a
# PROCESSED build — pilot silently SKIPS distribution when the wait is
# skipped. Default 90 min; override with TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
def testflight_wait_timeout
  seconds = ENV["TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"].to_i
  seconds.positive? ? seconds : 5400
end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }
  UI.user_error!("TestFlight external group '#{group}' (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP) not found in App Store Connect — create it or fix the repo variable. Nothing was uploaded.") if found.empty?
  [app, found.first]
end

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).
- Related: #1600 (closed via #1663 today), #1262 (CLI leg size budget — separate red leg blocking publish).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a

name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL fails the leg — same gate
      # family as the macOS pass (#1227). Eviction is pinned separately by

      # re-adds above 5% of TOTAL (Symbols/ qualifies at 99 MB; the 5.6 MB

      # artifact fails via --forbid in the same step. Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$MANIFEST"' EXIT
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv \
            --forbid '^Symbols/' --forbid 'coach_anny\.glb$' \
            --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1
            }
          done
          grep -q "LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm" "$MANIFEST" || {
            echo "::error::LiteRtLm.framework missing from the IPA — on-device LLM stack must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "✅ wasm runtime + LiteRT keep-set present; iOS size ratchet green"

      - name: Verify IPA and FFI symbols
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "IPA built successfully: $(ls -la "$IPA_PATH")"

          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$CHECK_DIR"
          PLIST=$(echo "$CHECK_DIR"/Payload/*.app/Info.plist)
          EXEC_NAME=$(plutil -extract CFBundleExecutable raw "$PLIST")
          BIN="$(dirname "$PLIST")/$EXEC_NAME"
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

          # cupertino_http trampolines (_NativeCupertinoHttp_*) live in a
          # static pod framework nothing native references; without the
          # Podfile force_load the Release link drops them and every network
          # call fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found'). Gate on it here so a
          # broken IPA never reaches TestFlight again.
          CUPERTINO_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " __NativeCupertinoHttp_" || true)
          echo "cupertino_http _NativeCupertinoHttp_* exports in binary: $CUPERTINO_COUNT"
          if [ "$CUPERTINO_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols exported from the app binary — networking via NSURLSession would fail at runtime"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ cupertino_http FFI symbols are exported"
          rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR"

      - name: Cleanup
        if: always()
        run: |
          security delete-keychain build.keychain || true
          rm -f certificate.p12

# Fastfile for the Fa app (flutter_app).
#
# TestFlight submit lanes, adapted 1:1 from learn.ai's deploy setup: builds
# happen in the CI workflows (flutter build ipa / flutter build macos), so
# these lanes only upload the produced artifacts with the App Store Connect
# API key from the environment:
#
# The daily's submit_only lanes distribute straight to the EXTERNAL
# TestFlight group (issue #239): the group name and Beta App Review contact
# ride repo variables (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_*,
# BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL). release-appstore.yml drives the manual
# submit_for_review lanes (App Store review submission).
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID / APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID /
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT
#
# Android (#289): the build_only/build_release + upload_only lanes follow
# the same split against Google Play; the service-account JSON rides
# PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON and
# the track rides PLAY_TRACK (internal first, then external beta).
#
# iOS:    IOS_IPA_PATH points at the built .ipa (default: build/ios/*.ipa's
#         conventional location).
# macOS:  MACOS_PKG_PATH points at the signed .pkg (Mac Installer
#         Distribution cert) and MACOS_BUNDLE_ID overrides dev.fa1.app.

require_relative "appstore_preflight"
require_relative "play_listing_sync"
require_relative "play_upload_preflight"
require_relative "store_version_create"
require_relative "version_floor"

def asc_api_key
  app_store_connect_api_key(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key_content: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"],
    is_key_content_base64: false,
    in_house: false
  )
end

# App Store locale map for the store pipeline: fastlane/metadata folder →
# App Store Connect locale. Golden screenshots live one level below under
# the plain language code (test/goldens/store/<en|ru>/<ios|ipad|mac>).
def store_locale_map
  { "en-US" => "en-US", "ru-RU" => "ru" }
end

# Latest "## [version]" section of store_artefacts/metadata/<lang>/changelog.md.
def store_latest_changelog(lang)
  file_path = File.expand_path("../../store_artefacts/metadata/#{lang}/changelog.md", __dir__)
  return "" unless File.exist?(file_path)
  content = File.read(file_path)
  match = content.match(/## \[.*?\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=\n## \[|\z)/m)
  match ? match[1].strip : ""
end

# gh-1522: the version string every store lane reports/verifies. The
# derived BUILD_NAME env (build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml version job,
# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# ── External TestFlight distribution (issue #239) ─────────────────────────
# A missing repo variable is a LOUD named failure at lane start (AC1) —
# never a fastlane stack trace mid-upload. The variables are set once as
# repo variables and passed through by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml.
def require_env!(name, what)
  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

def external_testflight_group!
  require_env!("TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP",
               "external TestFlight distribution needs the group name (create the 'External Beta' group in App Store Connect, then set the TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP repo variable)")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

# Issue #289 AC1 — Android release id guard. Plain ruby, no gems (runs on

# applicationId is IMMUTABLE after the first Play Console upload, so this

# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  repo_root = File.expand_path("../../..", __dir__)
  app_gradle = File.join(repo_root, "flutter_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts")

  $checks = 0
  def ok(message)
    $checks += 1
    puts "  ok: #{message}"

  raise "FAIL: #{app_gradle} not found" unless File.exist?(app_gradle)
  gradle = File.read(app_gradle)

# gh-1692: [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), routing still unpinned

## Description

### Bug

No TestFlight build has shipped since 2026-10-13 (5 daily-publish runs red). Investigation across the 5 failing runs shows FOUR distinct failure signatures, the last one current and untracked:

| Date | Runner | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| 10-14 | Linux box | routing bug, exit 127 (`bundle: command not found`) — #1600 L1, fixed by #1663 (merged 10-18 08:38) |
| 10-15 | gh-sandbox-agents-Mac-mini | wrong Mac (no signing env) — same routing class |
| 10-16 | fa-m5-1 | **IPA built OK**; submit leg died on transient git mirror fetch (`2876 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) |
| 10-17, 10-18 | fa-m5-2 | `** ARCHIVE FAILED **` in fastlane `build_app`, ~6s after clean, with xcpretty printing NO error line (runs 39006178578, 39100442363) |

### Current root cause (10-17/10-18): fa-m5-2 archive environment

- `flutter build ios --release` succeeds (158MB Runner.app); the xcodebuild archive invocation dies within seconds — the classic signature of a signing/keychain/profile problem on that machine (provisioning profiles "Fa Profile"/"FaLiveActivity Profile", manual signing, teamID YP9HC3USZ3). The full error lives in `~/Library/Logs/gym/Runner-Runner.log` ON fa-m5-2 — invisible from GitHub.
- The merged routing fix #1663 uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — this matches BOTH fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (failing), and possibly the sandbox Mac-mini if it advertises those labels. Tomorrow's run is a coin flip. #1600 AC1 wanted the jobs pinned to the known-good runner (`fa-m5-1`).

### Fix

1. **Pin iOS build+submit jobs to fa-m5-1** (runner-name label) until fa-m5-2's signing environment is verified — or fix fa-m5-2 (install/refresh the distribution cert + both provisioning profiles; verify with a manual `xcodebuild archive` on that box).
2. **Never-again (observability)**: fastlane itself warns xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" — switch the formatter to `xcbeautify` AND on failure upload `~/Library/Logs/gym/*.log` as a job artifact, so the next archive failure is diagnosable from the GH run page without shell access to the runner.
3. **Never-again (transient)**: the mirror-fetch in the submit leg needs a bounded retry (10-16 exit 128 was a pure network hiccup and cost a whole day of TestFlight).
4. Routing regression guard (#1600 AC1's workflow-lint) should assert iOS jobs resolve to the intended runner LABEL SET, not merely "a macOS ARM64 machine".

### Acceptance criteria

1. Next daily-publish ships a TestFlight build (iOS legs on the pinned/verified runner).
2. An archive failure surfaces the real xcodebuild error in the GH log or a failure artifact — no more silent `ARCHIVE FAILED`.
3. Mirror-fetch retry in the submit leg.

### Evidence

- Runs: 38516656653 (10-14), 38686834918 (10-15), 38855794448 (10-16, build green on fa-m5-1 + submit exit 128), 39006178578 + 39100442363 (10-17/18, fa-m5-2 ARCHIVE FAILED).
- Related: #1600 (closed via #1663 today), #1262 (CLI leg size budget — separate red leg blocking publish).

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo + extension
#                                 + the /outlook add-in slice)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-se…

# un-stripped copy still beats no artifact for debugging).
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH.stripped" {} +)
          mv -f "$IPA_PATH.stripped" "$IPA_PATH"
          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact
        # Uploaded before the symbol gate so a failed gate still leaves the
        # IPA available for debugging.
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/*.ipa
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 ratchet: per-file uncompressed floor seeded from the last
      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL fails the leg — same gate
      # family as the macOS pass (#1227). Eviction is pinned separately by
      # the --forbid deny-list: the NEW-line guard alone only catches
      # re-adds above 5% of TOTAL (Symbols/ qualifies at 99 MB; the 5.6 MB
      # glb does not — +3.8% TOTAL, sub-share NEW), so a returning evicted
      # artifact fails via --forbid in the same step. Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$MANIFEST"' EXIT
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv \
            --forbid '^Symbols/' --forbid 'coach_anny\.glb$' \
            --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1
            }
          done
          grep -q "LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm" "$MANIFEST" || {
            echo "::error::LiteRtLm.framework missing from the IPA — on-device LLM stack must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "✅ wasm runtime + LiteRT keep-set present; iOS size ratchet green"

      - name: Verify IPA and FFI symbols
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "IPA built successfully: $(ls -la "$IPA_PATH")"

          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported

          CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$CHECK_DIR"
          PLIST=$(echo "$CHECK_DIR"/Payload/*.app/Info.plist)

          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").

          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"

            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"

            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

          # static pod framework nothing native references; without the
          # Podfile force_load the Release link drops them and every network
          # call fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found'). Gate on it here so a
          # broken IPA never reaches TestFlight again.
          CUPERTINO_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " __NativeCupertinoHttp_" || true)
          echo "cupertino_http _NativeCupertinoHttp_* exports in binary: $CUPERTINO_COUNT"
          if [ "$CUPERTINO_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols exported from the app binary — networking via NSURLSession would fail at runtime"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ cupertino_http FFI symbols are exported"
          rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR"

        if: always()
        run: |
          security delete-keychain build.keychain || true
          rm -f certificate.p12

# Fastfile for the Fa app (flutter_app).
#
# TestFlight submit lanes, adapted 1:1 from learn.ai's deploy setup: builds
# happen in the CI workflows (flutter build ipa / flutter build macos), so
# these lanes only upload the produced artifacts with the App Store Connect
# API key from the environment:
#
# The daily's submit_only lanes distribute straight to the EXTERNAL
# TestFlight group (issue #239): the group name and Beta App Review contact
# ride repo variables (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_*,
# BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL). release-appstore.yml drives the manual
# submit_for_review lanes (App Store review submission).
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID / APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID /
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT
#
# Android (#289): the build_only/build_release + upload_only lanes follow
# the same split against Google Play; the service-account JSON rides
# PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON and
# the track rides PLAY_TRACK (internal first, then external beta).
#
# iOS:    IOS_IPA_PATH points at the built .ipa (default: build/ios/*.ipa's
#         conventional location).
# macOS:  MACOS_PKG_PATH points at the signed .pkg (Mac Installer
#         Distribution cert) and MACOS_BUNDLE_ID overrides dev.fa1.app.

require_relative "appstore_preflight"
require_relative "play_listing_sync"
require_relative "play_upload_preflight"
require_relative "store_version_create"
require_relative "version_floor"

def asc_api_key
  app_store_connect_api_key(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key_content: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"],
    is_key_content_base64: false,
    in_house: false
  )
end

# App Store locale map for the store pipeline: fastlane/metadata folder →
# App Store Connect locale. Golden screenshots live one level below under
# the plain language code (test/goldens/store/<en|ru>/<ios|ipad|mac>).
def store_locale_map
  { "en-US" => "en-US", "ru-RU" => "ru" }
end

# Latest "## [version]" section of store_artefacts/metadata/<lang>/changelog.md.
def store_latest_changelog(lang)
  file_path = File.expand_path("../../store_artefacts/metadata/#{lang}/changelog.md", __dir__)
  return "" unless File.exist?(file_path)
  content = File.read(file_path)
  match = content.match(/## \[.*?\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=\n## \[|\z)/m)
  match ? match[1].strip : ""
end

# gh-1522: the version string every store lane reports/verifies. The
# derived BUILD_NAME env (build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml version job,
# from the latest tag + 1) wins — the committed pubspec carries the static
# 0.0.0-dev placeholder now, so the pubspec parse is only the LAST-resort
# fallback (a hand-run lane outside the CI env).
def store_pubspec_version
  derived = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
  return derived unless derived.empty?
  pubspec_path = File.expand_path("../pubspec.yaml", __dir__)
  return "1.0.0" unless File.exist?(pubspec_path)
  match = File.read(pubspec_path).match(/version:\s+([0-9.]+)/)
  match ? match[1] : "1.0.0"
end

# ── External TestFlight distribution (issue #239) ─────────────────────────
# A missing repo variable is a LOUD named failure at lane start (AC1) —
# never a fastlane stack trace mid-upload. The variables are set once as
# repo variables and passed through by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml.
def require_env!(name, what)
  value = ENV[name].to_s.strip
  UI.user_error!("#{name} is not set — #{what}") if value.empty?
  value
end

def external_testflight_group!
  require_env!("TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP",
               "external TestFlight distribution needs the group name (create the 'External Beta' group in App Store Connect, then set the TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP repo variable)")
end

# Beta App Review contact (AC2): external distribution only flips green
# unattended when the review info is complete. The app is local-first —
# it boots without any account or key, so no demo account is required.
def beta_app_review_info!
  {
    contact_first_name: ENV.fetch("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_FIRST_NAME", "Uladzimir"),
    contact_last_name: ENV.fetch("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_LAST_NAME", "Klyshevich"),
    contact_email: require_env!("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL", "Beta App Review needs a contact email (set the BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL repo variable)"),
    contact_phone: require_env!("BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE", "Beta App Review needs a contact phone (set the BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE repo variable)"),
    demo_account_required: false,
    notes: "Local-first AI agent app. No account, sign-in or API key is required — the app boots fully on-device with local models, so there is nothing to sign into."
  }
end

def beta_app_feedback_email!
  require_env!("BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL", "external TestFlight testing needs a feedback email (set the BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL repo variable)")
end

# distribute_external requires a "What to Test" changelog — pilot raises in
# non-interactive CI without one. Reuse the store release notes.
def testflight_changelog
  notes = store_latest_changelog("en")
  notes.empty? ? "Bug fixes and improvements." : notes
end

# Bounded wait for ASC processing (E1): external distribution needs a
# PROCESSED build — pilot silently SKIPS distribution when the wait is
# skipped. Default 90 min; override with TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
def testflight_wait_timeout
  seconds = ENV["TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"].to_i
  seconds.positive? ? seconds : 5400
end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }

end
